title: Craftsman trace line, schema v1
description: One line of a Craftsman trace file (JSON Lines, schema id craftsman-harness/trace@1). This schema validates a single line and is the writer-side contract: a writer's tests fail on a value it does not list. A collector reads tolerantly instead (unknown enumeration values mean unknown, unknown fields and kinds are ignored) and uses the schema for diagnostics only; see docs/trace-schema-v1.md, section 3. The file-level rules (seq gap-free from 0, run_start first, run_end last, one run_id per file, hunk consistency) are in section 5.6 of that document and are checked by docs/schemas/check_trace.py. No object here sets additionalProperties to false, and a line of an unknown kind passes the envelope check.

seq.description: Position of the line in the file, counting from 0 with no gaps.

ts.description: RFC 3339 UTC with exactly three fractional digits (truncated, not rounded), taken when the recorded event completed.

run_id.description: Opaque id of the run; the same on every line of a file.

thread_id.description: The conversation thread of the run, or null when the run has none (for example an ephemeral run).

tree_hash_skipped.description: Why a tree hash is absent: git could not be started, git failed (this includes a directory that is not a git work tree), the 20 second budget ran out, or the writer had already stopped and did not try.

hunk.description: [old_start, old_len, new_start, new_len]: a run of lines of the old file (old_len lines from old_start) replaced by a run of the new file (new_len lines from new_start). Starts are 1-based; for a side with length 0 the start is the number of the line that follows the gap. Both lengths are never 0.

model.description: The model id the run was configured with.

harness_profile.description: The active harness profile key, for example general, openai, claude or nemotron.

cwd_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the absolute working directory. The path itself is never written.

tools.description: Names of the tools offered to the main agent's model, sorted ascending. An empty list means the start is unknown (the first line was a compaction call).

entry.description: How the run was started: one-shot for craftsman -m, exec for craftsman exec.

producer.description: The program that wrote the file: its name, version and, when the build knows it, the source commit.

tree_hash.description: Tree hash of the working directory when the run started.

tree_hash_ms.description: Milliseconds spent on the start tree hash, whether or not it succeeded.

model.description: The model id this provider was configured with. Optional; when absent, run_start.model applies.

cached_input_tokens.description: Optional: the part of input_tokens the provider served from a prompt cache. Absent when unknown (always absent in the instrumented baseline).

reasoning_tokens.description: Optional: the part of output_tokens spent on reasoning. Absent when unknown (always absent in the instrumented baseline).

usage_source.description: reported: the provider sent usage. estimated: the harness counted the tokens itself. missing: neither, and both token counts are null.

finish_reason.description: The provider's finish reason, or null when none was given or the call failed.

error.description: Present, and true, only when the call failed. Then finish_reason is null and usage_source is missing. Absent means the call succeeded; false is never written.

round.description: Index of the main-agent round during which the call ran.

call_id.description: The model's tool-call id, when the writer knows it.

argument_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the arguments the tool received.

output_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 text the model saw as the tool result.

output_body_sha256.description: Present only when the result ends with a block the harness appended (the stale-todo reminder): SHA-256 of the text without that block.

redacted.description: True when a redactor changed the result before the model saw it.

bytes.description: Length in bytes of the UTF-8 text hashed in output_sha256.

output_truncated.description: True when the tool cut its result at the output budget (the text ends, before any harness reminder, with the truncation marker).

exit_code.description: execute only: the exit status of the command. Absent means unknown; null is not used.

path.description: write_file and edit_file only: the target file, relative to the working directory with / separators when it lies inside it.

sha256_before.description: write_file and edit_file only: SHA-256 of the file bytes before the call, or null when the file did not exist.

sha256_after.description: write_file and edit_file only: SHA-256 of the file bytes after the call, or null when the file does not exist.

hunks.description: write_file and edit_file only: what the call changed, as hunks from the old file to the new file (section 6.8). Empty when the bytes are equal.

tree_hash.description: Tree hash of the working directory at the end of the round. Optional; absent in the instrumented baseline.

tree_hash_ms.description: Milliseconds spent on this round's tree hash. Optional; absent in the instrumented baseline.

tree_hash.description: Tree hash of the working directory when the run ended.

tree_hash_ms.description: Milliseconds spent on the end tree hash, whether or not it succeeded. Not part of wall_ms.
